EARLY-CLOSE RULE (settled here, applied to 2022, 2023 and 2024 alike). A family's status on date D is read only from what the document prints for D itself, and the comparison instant is that family's ordinary final close as printed in the SAME document for an adjacent regular trade date - never carried over from another document or another year. 'closed': the document prints no session running through D at all - neither a D-dated trade date nor a next-business-day-dated session that is open across D; the only instants printed in D's column, if any, are the evening reopen that ends the closure. 'early_close': D's own trade date ends strictly earlier than the family's ordinary final-close instant. 'late_open': it starts later. 'modified': D's printed instants are the family's ordinary ones but something else printed for D is non-normal - in these documents that is almost always D carrying no trade date of its own, the session running through D being labelled with the next business day's trade date while the family still halts and reopens at its ordinary instants. 'normal': nothing printed for D differs from the family's ordinary day; the trade date of the evening reopen that begins after D's close belongs to the next day's row, not D's. Under this rule the 16:00 CT holiday halt that CME prints for FX and CRYPTOCURRENCIES on holiday Mondays and Thursdays is NOT an early close - 16:00 CT is exactly the ordinary final close those two families print on the adjacent regular trade date in the same sheet, one-pager or service response - so 28 entries that round 0 recorded as 'early_close' at 16:00 CT are now 'modified' (2022-01-17, 2022-02-21, 2022-05-30, 2022-06-20, 2022-07-04, 2022-09-05, 2022-11-24, 2023-05-29, 2023-06-19, 2023-07-04, 2023-09-04, 2023-11-23, 2024-09-02 and 2024-11-28, globex_fx and globex_cryptocurrency on each). The 2023-07-03 and 2024-12-31 rows that print 16:00 (CLOSED) for a trade date of their own stay 'normal', which is what the same rule gives; the inconsistency the verifier found between the two cases is resolved by the rule, not by moving one of them.
